title: Windows cleanup research catalogue
scope: Windows 10/11 desktop baseline, optional Microsoft apps and enterprise features, plus explicitly marked historical/discovery candidates. Not an exhaustive list of every app, server role, OS build or relocated cache.
status: Research/design catalogue, not executable or production-validated deletion policy.

global_policy.timestamps: Suggested age uses LastWriteTimeUtc, not LastAccessTime. Age alone does not prove a file unused.
global_policy.directory_handling: Evaluate files individually; remove only now-empty subdirectories after validation. Never recursive-delete a directory merely because its own timestamp is old.
required_checks: Validate target identity and allowlisted root
Skip unresolved variables and absent locations
Revalidate against reparse-point swaps at deletion time
Exclude active installation/servicing/sync and recovery work
Skip sharing violations/access denied and log them
global_policy.shipping_guidance: Keep discover_only and exclude rows non-executable. Enabling other methods requires an implemented, tested adapter and applicable user selection.

path_notation.percent_variables: Resolve for selected user/environment; not necessarily cleaner process.
path_notation.braces: Logical placeholders requiring a resolver; not Windows environment variables.
path_notation.wildcards: Documentation patterns only, not shell commands. Restrict enumeration to validated roots.
path_notation.locations: Discovery hints. A location in this file is NOT permission to recursively delete it.

methods.filtered_contents: Future file adapter, individual selection with all gates.
methods.windows_cleanup: OS cleanup category/handler; do not translate to rm/rmdir.
methods.owner_api: Supported owning component API; semantic, not an implementation.
methods.owner_ui: Delegate to owning application or Windows UI.
methods.command: Dispatch a documented command only through a tested adapter.
methods.repair_workflow: Separate version-tested repair procedure with explicit scope.

groups.Temporary files: Candidates for conservative file-level retention, after per-rule gates; no unconditional safe-delete claim.
groups.Rebuildable caches: Optional reclamation; regeneration has a cost. Use owner cleanup when available.
groups.Diagnostic retention: Optional old diagnostic evidence; preserve newest samples and active investigations.
groups.Windows-managed cleanup: Windows or management product selects/removes its own content.
groups.Repair only: Explicit troubleshooting action, never run during ordinary disk cleanup.
groups.Application-specific: Separate version-aware application adapter; not universal Windows rules.
groups.Privacy only: User-selected history removal; distinguish from disk hygiene.
groups.User-selected data: Real user files/content; separate informed selection.
groups.Protected or excluded: Never a generic deletion target; exceptions require a separate specific workflow.

rules.label: Resolved user temporary directory
rules.notes: Resolve under target user token; preserve root and ACLs. Old files can still be needed; skip active workloads and recovery data. TMP and TEMP may differ.

rules.label: Conventional local user temp
rules.notes: Fallback/discovery candidate; deduplicate against resolved temp. Do not assume it is the only user temp path.

rules.label: Windows temporary directory
rules.notes: Privileged scope; only stale contents when installations/servicing are idle. Skip protected or inaccessible entries.

rules.label: SYSTEM temporary directory
rules.notes: GetTempPath2 under SYSTEM uses SystemTemp override or documented C:\Windows\SystemTemp default. Ordinary user resolution does not reveal this path. Preserve restrictive ACLs.

rules.label: LocalService temporary directory
rules.notes: Specialist service cleanup only; keep default off and avoid running service work.

rules.label: NetworkService temporary directory
rules.notes: Same service safeguards; do not sweep the surrounding profile.

rules.label: System profile temporary directory
rules.notes: Exists on some installations; distinguish native System32 from redirected access.

rules.label: 32-bit system profile temp candidate
rules.notes: Only if this is a distinct existing directory; deduplicate by filesystem identity.

rules.label: Packaged app temporary storage
rules.notes: Enumerate installed packages for selected user; exclude active apps and pending captures/recovery work. Never remove package root.

rules.label: Configured alternate temporary directories
rules.notes: Include per-user TMP/TEMP overrides and terminal-session temp paths only after validating ownership, root boundaries, and exclusions. Never trust an arbitrary environment value as deletion authority.

rules.label: Explorer thumbnails
rules.notes: Use Windows Thumbnails cleanup category; selective files only for a separately validated shell adapter. Regeneration costs time.

rules.label: Explorer icon cache
rules.notes: Rebuild only for icon problems, with a planned Explorer restart; never delete all Explorer databases.

rules.label: DirectX shader cache
rules.notes: Prefer DirectX Shader Cache category exposed on the target build. Close graphics workloads; next launches may compile shaders again.

rules.label: SYSTEM DirectX shader cache candidate
rules.notes: Specialist coverage candidate; do not enable generic SYSTEM graphics-cache deletion.

rules.label: Legacy WinINet temporary internet files
rules.notes: Enumerate/filter cache entries with WinINet APIs or Windows cleanup. The parent may contain Office attachment work; do not recursively purge it.

rules.label: Legacy WebCache database
rules.notes: Not a generic disposable folder; associated cache/history state can be coordinated by other components. Use owner-specific cleanup.

rules.label: Legacy downloaded program components
rules.notes: Use the Downloaded Program Files handler if present; do not directly delete installed legacy components.

rules.label: Microsoft Store cache
rules.notes: Run wsreset.exe in the affected user context for Store problems. Do not replace this with removal of the Store package folder.

rules.label: Windows font cache candidates
rules.notes: Font-related repair only. Requires service-aware, version-tested sequence; do not stop services during ordinary cleaning.

rules.label: Windows Search index
rules.notes: Use Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild for corruption, or reduce indexed locations. Report allocated size. Do not remove database files in generic cleanup.

rules.label: Application crash dumps
rules.notes: Read WER LocalDumps configuration for overrides. Preserve newest evidence and keep if troubleshooting; delete only selected completed dumps.

rules.label: Configured service crash dumps
rules.notes: Service accounts can use profile-specific dump folders. Resolve actual LocalDumps settings and do not assume current user path.

rules.label: System crash memory dump
rules.notes: Resolve CrashControl DumpFile override. Preserve the latest dump until the cause has been diagnosed.

rules.label: System minidumps
rules.notes: Resolve configured destination; retain recent crashes and newest useful sample.

rules.label: Live kernel reports
rules.notes: Select completed .dmp files in subfolders; do not remove folders or unrelated contents. These can diagnose failures without a full system crash.

rules.label: Machine WER archives
rules.notes: Completed archived reports; prefer available WER cleanup handler. Archive/report folder is the deletion unit.

rules.label: Machine WER queue
rules.notes: May contain unsent diagnostic evidence; separately selected cleanup only after review.

rules.label: Machine WER staging
rules.notes: Do not race report collection/upload. Use Windows cleanup where supported.

rules.label: Per-user WER report candidates
rules.notes: Version-dependent candidates, verify on target build; prefer per-user WER handlers when available.

rules.label: Archived CBS servicing logs
rules.notes: Only completed CbsPersist archives; keep CBS.log and newest useful archive. Avoid servicing and unresolved update errors.

rules.label: DISM logs
rules.notes: Retain active dism.log; offer only individually reviewed rotated logs after servicing is complete. Never blanket-delete Logs.

rules.label: Windows Setup logs
rules.notes: Setup log files category when available; no whole-Panther deletion. Preserve upgrade troubleshooting evidence.

rules.label: Device installation logs
rules.notes: Diagnostic files, not a cache. Preserve active logs; a retention adapter must identify completed rotations.

rules.label: Windows event logs
rules.notes: Do not wipe event logs for disk hygiene. Explicit log administration uses Event Viewer/wevtutil and separate retention/export policies.

rules.label: Downloaded Windows Update payloads
rules.notes: Windows cleanup first. Manual reset is a separate repair workflow; do not delete while download/install or reboot completion is pending.

rules.label: Windows Update datastore
rules.notes: Do not routinely clean database or transaction logs. Microsoft documents reset as troubleshooting; this is not uninstalling installed updates.

rules.label: Cryptographic catalog database
rules.notes: Only a documented update repair, preserving service state. Never apply the same operation to catroot.

rules.label: Delivery Optimization cache
rules.notes: Query cache/jobs using DO cmdlets. Use Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache; omit IncludePinnedFiles in ordinary cleanup. Location may be policy-relocated.

rules.label: Component store
rules.notes: Use DISM AnalyzeComponentStore / StartComponentCleanup. No recursive deletion, including WinSxS\Temp. Exclude ResetBase from routine maintenance.

rules.label: Previous Windows installation
rules.notes: Explicit selection; inspect for recoverable user files and explain rollback loss. Use Previous Windows installation(s).

rules.label: Upgrade staging / rollback folders
rules.notes: Build/setup-dependent locations; Windows temporary installation cleanup only after successful upgrade and rollback review. Do not force ownership.

rules.label: Installation/recovery image candidates
rules.notes: May contain recovery or installation sources. Identify role and owner first; never an automatic junk rule.

rules.label: Superseded driver packages
rules.notes: Only OS-supported Device driver packages cleanup when exposed. Manual driver removal belongs to driver management, not file deletion.

rules.label: BranchCache content
rules.notes: Optional enterprise feature; use Clear-BCCache after detecting module and policy. Re-fetching affects network usage.

rules.label: Configuration Manager content cache
rules.notes: Actual cache path is configurable. Use Configuration Manager cache controls; raw filesystem deletion breaks cache bookkeeping.

rules.label: Recycle Bin
rules.notes: Use SHEmptyRecycleBin / supported shell interface for whole-bin cleanup. Explicit selection; no deletion of other users bins. Age-selective removal needs a separate shell-item implementation.

rules.label: Downloads
rules.notes: User documents and installers, not junk. Manual review only; never enable by default. Resolve redirected known folder.

rules.label: OneDrive/cloud local copies
rules.notes: Use provider Free up space/dehydration after confirming synced state. DeleteFile can delete cloud data, not just a local cache.

rules.label: Printer spool jobs
rules.notes: Live print jobs, not junk. Explicit cancellation/recovery only. Discover configured spool directory; never sweep spool drivers.

rules.label: Microsoft Edge browser HTTP cache
rules.notes: Resolve actual profiles and cache overrides; use Cached images and files setting. No entire User Data or profile deletion. Background Edge processes must be idle for any future file adapter.

rules.label: Browser compiled-code and GPU cache candidates
rules.notes: Version-specific adapter needed; do not infer every Cache directory is disposable. Preserve session, cookie and credential stores.

rules.label: WebView2 cache
rules.notes: Owning application can clear selected browsing-data kinds using WebView2 APIs. Entire UDF contains cookies/settings and other persistent data. No systemwide UDF wipe.

rules.label: New Teams cache
rules.notes: Use documented Teams cache procedure after Quit. This specific vendor rule is not permission to purge other LocalCache folders.

rules.label: Classic Teams cache / state
rules.notes: Legacy version only: verify installed client and use documented reset after Quit. Treat as reset, not routine application cache cleaning.

rules.label: Office document cache
rules.notes: May hold pending document work. Use supported Office retention/repair workflows after verifying all changes saved and synchronized. Version/path may differ.

rules.label: Office web add-in cache
rules.notes: Use current host-specific Office add-in instructions; do not assume both paths apply to every host. Close relevant Office apps.

rules.label: Classic Outlook attachment working files
rules.notes: Resolve OutlookSecureTempFolder for the installed version. Check for unsaved attachment edits; not an unconditional temporary-file rule.

rules.label: Recent-document shortcuts
rules.notes: Clear Recent items through shell settings/appropriate interfaces. This removes history, not original documents; retain pinned preferences.

rules.label: Jump Lists / Quick Access state
rules.notes: May also store pinned items. Do not call a raw folder wipe cache cleaning.

rules.label: Clipboard and clipboard history
rules.notes: User content, potentially synchronized. Use Windows clipboard controls; not a disk-temp directory.

rules.label: DNS resolver cache
rules.notes: ipconfig /flushdns for name-resolution troubleshooting. Not a meaningful disk-space cleanup target.

rules.label: Prefetch
rules.notes: Exclude from routine cleaning; do not equate performance-related cache with disposable junk or promise speed gains.

rules.label: System Resource Usage database
rules.notes: Telemetry/accounting database, not an allowlisted temp folder. Community cleaners target it; this catalogue deliberately does not.

rules.label: Windows diagnostic traces
rules.notes: Owner-specific retention only. Some files are live traces or databases; no recursive wildcard log cleanup.

rules.label: WinSAT assessment data
rules.notes: Assessment output and logs; preserve by default. Any future rule must select obsolete outputs, not the whole directory.

rules.label: Legacy setup temporary directory
rules.notes: Historical/version-dependent candidate. Validate owner and stale setup state before adding a deletion rule.

rules.label: Device metadata cache backup
rules.notes: Community-observed backup candidate; verify target build. No general DeviceMetadataCache deletion.

rules.label: Windows Installer cache
rules.notes: Never generic-delete cached MSI/MSP or $PatchCache$. Missing payloads can break update, repair and uninstall later.

rules.label: Installer package caches
rules.notes: Owner-specific installer policy only. Visual Studio has a supported cache policy; do not extrapolate it to all bootstrapper caches.

rules.label: All packaged-app LocalCache folders
rules.notes: Persistent app data can include authentication tokens. Permit only narrower app-specific adapters with documented semantics.

rules.label: Packaged-app persistent state
rules.notes: User settings, application data and runtime state. Do not generically erase AC or database transaction logs either.

rules.label: Browser persistent storage
rules.notes: Offline web applications, sessions and cookies can live here. Explicit browser site-data reset is separate and may destroy offline work or log users out.

rules.label: Outlook mailbox and recovery data
rules.notes: No broad deletion of PST/OST, draft/recovery files or mail app databases. Data may not exist elsewhere.

rules.label: Windows persistent system stores
rules.notes: Critical OS state; a temp subdirectory under an explicitly identified system profile is a narrowly scoped exception, not authority over its parent.

rules.label: Recovery and restore storage
rules.notes: Recovery points, snapshots and recovery environment are not junk. Any retention change requires a separate supported recovery-management workflow.

rules.label: Paging, swap and hibernation files
rules.notes: Manage via Windows settings. Hibernation changes belong to power configuration and can affect Fast Startup; never direct-delete these files.

rules.label: Sync databases and security state
rules.notes: Conservative exclusions: no generic deletion of synchronization state, protection history/quarantine, cryptographic keys, credentials or tokens.

rules.label: Drive-wide extension sweeps
rules.notes: A suffix does not establish ownership or disposability. CAB can be installation content; logs can be database transaction logs; TMP can be active or recovery data.

rules.label: Certificate URL cache
rules.notes: Certificate URL/CRL cache; certutil -URLcache lists entries. Targeted deletion is troubleshooting only and can require refetching certificate validation data. Operate in the intended user context.

rules.label: Service certificate URL caches
rules.notes: Inventory only; service-context caches are not cleared by running a user-context command. No direct recursive deletion.

rules.label: Windows Update ETW traces
rules.notes: Trace data helps diagnose update failures. Retention requires identifying completed sessions; do not blindly erase live ETL files.

rules.label: Update Orchestrator traces
rules.notes: Diagnostic retention candidate, not a payload cache. Protect ongoing update analysis and active traces.
